platform.name: Example multi-asset platform
platform.description: Example scope showing both supported web target forms: an absolute service URL and asset host/IP plus service port/protocol/base path.

authorization.reference: Replace with the real authorization/ticket/reference and set confirmed=true before executing a real assessment. This example enables discovered same-host/same-scheme multi-port scope.

portal_primary.purpose: Primary OIDC web identity. An existing cookie is tried first on its configured origin and on discovered same-host/same-scheme ports only when allow_same_host_ports=true; it is never copied to a different hostname. If validation fails, saved browser/OIDC state is tried and the original username/password may be reused only after the browser reaches the same issuer/realm. No second console prompt is opened.

services.notes: Absolute-URL form. When url is set it takes precedence over asset.host, service.port, protocol and base_path. portal_primary opts into authorized-sibling OIDC/SSO reuse: saved SSO state is tried first and the initially resolved username/password are reused automatically only after the browser reaches the same primary OIDC issuer/realm.
Host/IP + port form. This service resolves from asset.host plus port/protocol/base_path; omitting protocol would infer HTTP for port 80.

Host/IP + port form with explicit HTTPS because 8443 is a non-standard HTTPS port. It reuses portal_primary as an identity reference, but the runner obtains/validates a separate exact-origin application session for this sibling rather than copying the primary Cookie header.
The service is part of the platform inventory; the current web orchestrators record it as unsupported and do not test it.
